title: Whole tuning arguments constrained by converging paths and an exact interval discrepancy
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. A complete Sectio canonis example makes fourth times fifth equal an octave, while six 9:8 tones overshoot the same octave. Different variable-length tuning/proof accounts must share interval meanings and agree on every equality and discrepancy. This is an arithmetic and musical content network, not a copied melody, literal pes rotation or fixed seven-number record.

design.mechanism: One shared content semantics represents sounds, interval ratios, ordered tuning paths, inversions, co-references and assertions of equal or unequal endpoints. Repeated uses of one interval apply the same ratio. Alternative paths meeting a sound must reconcile; a stated residual must equal their ratio. A complete argument may contain variable numbers of instructions and proof clauses without changing these rules.
design.unit: A complete tuning or interval argument with starting state, alternative paths, comparisons, explanations and prerequisite calls. The owned example is Sectio canonis proposition IX, with complete second proof VI and propositions XII–XIV establishing the relevant musical ratio claims.
design.contrast: IDEA000135/GDT901 tested the complete fixed 22-pitch solmization operational register and excluded all ten frozen role partitions. IDEA000142 and the owned rota concern timed coordinated voices; GDT970 METHOD requires literal whole-pes glyph conjugacy under a concatenative event code. This proposal copies neither source output nor its order and has no glyph-rotation consequence. It introduces exact ratio identities and a source-owned nonzero discrepancy. No predecessor is repaired.
design.prediction: The same global meanings must satisfy fourth*fifth=octave, fifth/fourth=tone, and tone^6>octave when fourth=4/3, fifth=3/2, octave=2, tone=9/8 are bound. The source starts at262144; six tone steps reach531441, while doubling reaches524288. A rival declaring exact six-tone octave closure cannot satisfy the same ratio claims. Arbitrary new values at each node would destroy the shared-content hypothesis.

source_example.work: Sectio canonis, ancient Greek work transmitted under Euclid; attribution and precise date disputed
source_example.edition: Charles-Émile Ruelle French translation, collected edition1884; digitized by Marc Szwajcer. Owned title image actually viewed. No medieval witness of the precise passage acquired.
complete_IX_actions: State that six successive sesquioctave ratios exceed a double ratio.
Choose A and define B,G,D,E,Z,H as successive9:8 multiples.
Invoke Elements VIII.2 for constructing seven such integers.
Give all seven integers in order.
source_example.second_complete_path: VI second proof: A/B=3/2 and B/G=4/3; hence2A=3B=4G, soA=2G. XII identifies these as fifth, fourth and octave.
source_example.additional_written_claims: XII also gives octave-plus-fifth=3 and double octave=4. XIII identifies tone as the difference of fifth and fourth, ratio9:8. XIV concludes octave smaller than six tones.
source_example.written_vs_inferred: 524288 and7153 occur explicitly in Ruelle editorial footnote25, not in the ancient IX body. Residual ratio531441/524288 is our mathematical expression of the discrepancy. Exact rational calculation verified the entire written sequence and check values.
source_example.prerequisites: VI–XIV and introduction read, including the mathematical and consonance assumptions used by XII. Elements VIII.2 is explicitly cited but its full proof was not acquired. Boethius II.30 text layer corroborates octave/comma numbers, but its omitted diagram/table is not claimed acquired.
source_example.source_conflicts: Ruelle discloses a restored proposition betweenVI andVII and figure/label corrections elsewhere. No repaired figure is used for the selected second proofVI or numerical IX. No universal consonance/hearing law follows.

source_receipt.native_vision: Owned title image actually viewed; selected numerical proof is complete HTML text and table, not claimed medieval page geometry.

symmetries: If numerical values remain unbound, a common positive power transformation of every ratio preserves product/equality/order; a loop alone does not identify octave or frequency units.
Permutations of the same interval factors share an endpoint ratio while generally changing intermediate sounds. Endpoint closure alone does not identify instruction order.
design.scope: A source-supported content architecture with explicit closure and nonclosure, no target writing contract. Six successive source steps are a worked example, not a required unknown-text length. No tonal glyph code, instrument owner or translated noun is established.
design.writing_contract: Unknown. No cipher, source-copy order, fixed word/event count, fixed decimal/opcode fields or paragraph boundary rule is supplied. A future finite globally shared variable-length grammar must express all clauses in its declared complete scope, including explanations, conditions, references, endpoint comparisons and alternatives. These cannot become free padding.
design.structural_dependencies: Retain hierarchy at spaces, directed composition, whole-form residuals, position/entry effects, and ambiguity between alternative transcriptions. No identified phonetic alphabet or default Latin basis. Joint whole-reading hypotheses remain allowed without a known word.
design.ownership_limit: No complete admitted target owner or independent target consequence is nominated. Missing writing design is not empirical failure or proof of absent meaning. No decoder or next target experiment is selected.
design.access: Required route, registry metadata and claim-bearing predecessor reports only for target context. No target corpus body, new Voynich image, reserve or outside contact accessed. Existing IDEA000349–352 and their source dossier remain unchanged.
